title: Two morphisms of coverings over the same morphism induce the same map on zeroth Cech sets
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be a site [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology] and $\mathcal F$ a presheaf of sets on $\mathcal C$. Let $\mathcal U=\{U_i\to U\}_{i\in I}$ and $\mathcal V=\{\rho_j:V_j\to V\}_{j\in J}$ be coverings, and let $f=(\chi,\alpha,(f_i)_{i\in I})$ and $g=(\chi,\beta,(g_i)_{i\in I})$ be two morphisms of coverings $\mathcal U\to\mathcal V$ lying over the same morphism $\chi:U\to V$ (so $f_i:U_i\to V_{\alpha(i)}$, $g_i:U_i\to V_{\beta(i)}$, $\rho_{\alpha(i)}f_i=\rho_{\beta(i)}g_i=\chi\circ(U_i\to U)$), with induced maps $f^*,g^*:H^0(\mathcal V,\mathcal F)\to H^0(\mathcal U,\mathcal F)$, $(f^*s)_i=\mathcal F(f_i)(s_{\alpha(i)})$, $(g^*s)_i=\mathcal F(g_i)(s_{\beta(i)})$, as in [def-weil-pbc-site-plus-construction] (a), (b). Then $f^*=g^*$. In particular, if $\mathcal U$ and $\mathcal V$ are coverings of the same object, every morphism of coverings $\mathcal U\to\mathcal V$ over the identity induces the same map $H^0(\mathcal V,\mathcal F)\to H^0(\mathcal U,\mathcal F)$.

source.place: Sites, Lemma 00W7 (lemma-independent-refinement) and its proof; Remark 00W8 (remark-both-refine-same-H0)

proof.text: *The morphism $\varphi_i$.* Write $\mathcal U=\{\pi_i:U_i\to U\}_{i\in I}$, $\mathcal V=\{\rho_j:V_j\to V\}_{j\in J}$. Fix $i\in I$. By the definition of a morphism of coverings [def-weil-pbc-site-plus-construction] (b), applied to $f$ and to $g$, which lie over the same $\chi$, $\rho_{\alpha(i)}\circ f_i=\chi\circ\pi_i=\rho_{\beta(i)}\circ g_i$. Let $V_{\alpha(i)}\times_VV_{\beta(i)}$ with projections $\mathrm{pr}_1,\mathrm{pr}_2$ be the fibre product [def-weil-pbc-category-fibre-product] of $\rho_{\alpha(i)}$ and $\rho_{\beta(i)}$ that appears in the definition of $H^0(\mathcal V,\mathcal F)$ [def-weil-pbc-site-plus-construction] (a) for the pair of indices $(\alpha(i),\beta(i))$ (it exists by axiom (iii) of a site [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology], applied to the covering $\mathcal V$ and the morphism $\rho_{\beta(i)}:V_{\beta(i)}\to V$; when $\alpha(i)=\beta(i)$ it is $V_{\alpha(i)}\times_VV_{\alpha(i)}$). By its universal property, with $T=U_i$, $x=f_i$, $y=g_i$, there is a (unique) morphism $\varphi_i:U_i\to V_{\alpha(i)}\times_VV_{\beta(i)}$ with $\mathrm{pr}_1\circ\varphi_i=f_i$ and $\mathrm{pr}_2\circ\varphi_i=g_i$.

*The two components agree.* Let $s=(s_j)_{j\in J}\in H^0(\mathcal V,\mathcal F)$ and $i\in I$. Since $\mathcal F$ is a functor $\mathcal C^{op}\to$ sets, $\mathcal F(u\circ v)=\mathcal F(v)\circ\mathcal F(u)$ for composable $u,v$. Hence, with $\varphi_i$ of step 1 and the formula for $f^*$, $g^*$ of [def-weil-pbc-site-plus-construction] (b), $(f^*s)_i=\mathcal F(f_i)(s_{\alpha(i)})=\mathcal F(\mathrm{pr}_1\circ\varphi_i)(s_{\alpha(i)})=\mathcal F(\varphi_i)\big(\mathcal F(\mathrm{pr}_1)(s_{\alpha(i)})\big)$ and $(g^*s)_i=\mathcal F(g_i)(s_{\beta(i)})=\mathcal F(\varphi_i)\big(\mathcal F(\mathrm{pr}_2)(s_{\beta(i)})\big)$. The defining condition of $H^0(\mathcal V,\mathcal F)$ [def-weil-pbc-site-plus-construction] (a) for the indices $j=\alpha(i)$, $j'=\beta(i)$ says $\mathcal F(\mathrm{pr}_1)(s_{\alpha(i)})=s_{\alpha(i)}|_{V_{\alpha(i)}\times_VV_{\beta(i)}}=s_{\beta(i)}|_{V_{\alpha(i)}\times_VV_{\beta(i)}}=\mathcal F(\mathrm{pr}_2)(s_{\beta(i)})$ in $\mathcal F(V_{\alpha(i)}\times_VV_{\beta(i)})$. Applying $\mathcal F(\varphi_i)$ gives $(f^*s)_i=(g^*s)_i$.

*Conclusion.* $f^*s$ and $g^*s$ are elements of $H^0(\mathcal U,\mathcal F)\subseteq\prod_{i\in I}\mathcal F(U_i)$ [def-weil-pbc-site-plus-construction] (a) whose components agree for every $i\in I$ by step 2, so $f^*s=g^*s$; as $s\in H^0(\mathcal V,\mathcal F)$ was arbitrary, $f^*=g^*$. The last sentence of the statement is the case $V=U$, $\chi=\mathrm{id}_U$: two morphisms of coverings $\mathcal U\to\mathcal V$ over $\mathrm{id}_U$ lie over the same morphism, so they induce the same map $H^0(\mathcal V,\mathcal F)\to H^0(\mathcal U,\mathcal F)$.
